answer: Let the network retarget identity creation cost as a dune reshapes in the wind: whenever new identities arrive faster than a slow baseline, the entry price per identity automatically rises, so a sybil operator minting a thousand fakes faces a steeply climbing bill per fake, while honest newcomers at a normal pace pay almost nothing. The rising fee acts as a public signal of an attack in progress, and the collected fees are burned, like cedar needles feeding no one, so the attacker cannot recover the cost. A single genuine agent is unaffected, but mass forgery becomes ruinously expensive.
